title: Mixed-race jamming; the white clarinetist 'Bonet'
summary: Black and white musicians mixed freely at the Entertainers; Handy recalls a friendly white player.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: Did the white musicians come in and mix it up then? Yes, indeed man. They always did that, huh? Always did that. Musicians always wanted to play together, didn't they?

It didn't make no difference. What? This boy named Ross Bonet? Mm-hmm. Oh man, him and I used to kick it back, man. What did he play? General Sykes, man. That's one of your greatest Sykes, wrong place.
Ross Bonet? Sure. I thought he was governor of Mississippi.

Oh, come on now. You must mean Charlie Bonet or something. Yeah, Charlie Bonet. You have to help me out a little bit, Dick. I'm trying to get you in bed. I couldn't let you get by with that. No, that's that one. That was the first job you played on Alton, you say? Yeah. First job I played on Alton. Just a mix-up band.
